skill.name: estat-stats
skill.description: e-Stat(政府統計の総合窓口)APIで統計表の検索・メタ情報・データ取得を行う。人口、GDP、CPI、統計、調査データに対応。無料のappId(APIキー)が必要。統計表をWebサイトで見たいだけの場合はe-Statのサイトを案内する。
skill.summary: Search Japanese government statistical tables, inspect metadata, and retrieve filtered values through the official e-Stat API.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: All 30 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, official e-Stat URLs, a documentation link, and readable Japanese text. No evidence found of prompt injection, malicious execution, or unauthorized data exfiltration. One separate concern remains: expanded API keys enter curl process arguments and may be visible to local process inspection or monitoring.

remediation.issue: API keys enter curl process arguments after environment variable expansion.
remediation.suggestion: Use an HTTP client that reads the key internally, or pass curl configuration through standard input; redact credential-bearing URLs from logs.

content.user_title: Find and Retrieve Japanese Government Statistics
content.value_statement: Japanese statistical tables use table identifiers and dimension codes that can be difficult to navigate. This skill guides table search, metadata inspection, and filtered retrieval through the official e-Stat API.
actual_capabilities: Guides keyword searches with getStatsList and identifies table IDs, titles, survey names, and responsible agencies.
Explains getMetaInfo responses to identify dimensions and map classification codes to labels.
Provides getStatsData examples with metadata-derived filters for population totals.
Describes paginated retrieval using limit, startPosition, and response counters.
Distinguishes authentication errors, parameter errors, empty results, timeouts, and service failures.
Explains appId setup, environment-variable storage, source attribution, bounded retries, and request pacing.
limitations: Live retrieval requires an e-Stat appId, network access, and an assistant with shell or HTTP tools.
The package contains instructions and curl examples, not a standalone client, analysis engine, or visualization tool.
Example table IDs and classification codes require verification against current metadata; statistical coverage depends on e-Stat.
The linked shared response checklist is not included in the package.

use_cases.title: Locate Population Tables
use_cases.description: Find relevant population tables and inspect their dimensions before retrieving research data.

use_cases.title: Check Official Economic Sources
use_cases.description: Search for GDP or CPI tables and identify official sources for a report.

use_cases.title: Retrieve Filtered Statistical Values
use_cases.description: Use metadata-derived codes and pagination to collect public statistics for a data workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Statistical Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Find up to five e-Stat population tables. Show their IDs, titles, and responsible agencies. Use my configured appId without displaying it.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Table Dimensions
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect metadata for e-Stat table [table ID]. Explain its dimensions and available region, time, and category codes before requesting values.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Filtered Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve [measure] from table [table ID] for [region] and [period]. Verify filter codes using metadata. Report labels, units, and source attribution.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Multiple Pages Reliably
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve all matching values from [table ID] using [filters]. Paginate with response counters, pace requests, check application status, and report incomplete retrieval.

output_examples.input: Explain the metadata needed to retrieve total population from the documented example table.
output: The skill uses table 0000150002 as its population-estimates example.
Its documented filters select total age and total sex using code 000 for both dimensions.
Confirm those codes with current metadata and map returned time and area codes to their labels.
Actual values require a live request with a valid appId.

output_examples.input: The request returned HTTP 200, but the application status is 100. Did retrieval succeed?
output: No. The documented status 100 indicates authentication failure even when HTTP status is 200.
Check that ESTAT_APP_ID is configured without printing its value.
Verify the appId in your e-Stat account before requesting data again.

best_practices: Keep the appId out of chat, commits, process arguments, and logs; use a credential-safe request method.
Inspect metadata before choosing filters, map codes to labels, and include official source attribution.
Check application status, apply timeouts, pace paginated requests, reuse results, and limit retries.
anti_patterns: Assuming HTTP 200 means the statistical request succeeded.
Reusing classification codes across tables without checking metadata.
Treating one limited response page as a complete dataset.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Obtain an appId through e-Stat registration and configure it outside chat or committed files.

faq.question: Which statistics can I search?
faq.answer: The skill targets e-Stat tables, including population, GDP, CPI, labor, and regional statistics. Availability depends on the service.

faq.question: Does this package include an executable client?
faq.answer: No. It provides API instructions and curl examples. Live requests require suitable tools and network access.

faq.question: Why inspect metadata before retrieving values?
faq.answer: Metadata defines each table's dimensions and classification codes. It helps select valid filters and interpret returned values.

faq.question: Can HTTP 200 still indicate failure?
faq.answer: Yes. Check the response application status. The skill documents status 100 for authentication failure and status 0 for success.

faq.question: Do retrieved statistics need attribution?
faq.answer: The skill states that outputs using retrieved data need source credit. Review the linked e-Stat attribution requirements.
